21718-the-big-otter.title: The Big Otter
21718-the-big-otter.creator: Unknown
21718-the-big-otter.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. This leading of the way through the trackless wilderness in snow averaging four feet deep is harder work than one might suppose. It could not be done at all without the aid of snow-shoes, which, varying from three to five feet in length, enable the traveller to walk on the surface of the snow, into which he would otherwise sink, more or less, according to its condition. If it be newly fallen and very soft, he sinks six, eight, or more inches.

42008-telling-fortunes-by-cards.title: Telling Fortunes By Cards
42008-telling-fortunes-by-cards.creator: Unknown
42008-telling-fortunes-by-cards.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. In our day and generation divination by cards is chiefly employed for amusement and pastime, for the entertainment of one's self or one's company, or at church fairs, charity bazars, and the like; but in the days of the ancients it was practiced by prophets and sibyls as a serious business, and so accepted by all, from king to peasant.

Duev, Matthew J. Graham, Thomas Kupfer, Frank J. Masci, Dan Reiley, Richard Walters, M. Dominik, U. G. Jørgensen, A. Andrews, N.
arxiv-2105-05826.description: Abstract Cometary activity is a manifestation of sublimation-driven processes at the surface of nuclei. However, cometary outbursts may arise from other processes that are not necessarily driven by volatiles. In order to fully understand nuclear surfaces and their evolution, we must identify the causes of cometary outbursts. In that context, we present a study of mini-outbursts of comet 46P/Wirtanen.

arxiv-2105-08102.title: Discrete minimal nets with symmetries
arxiv-2105-08102.creator: Joseph Cho, Wayne Rossman, Seong-Deog Yang
arxiv-2105-08102.description: Abstract . In this paper, we extend the notion of Schwarz reflection principle for smooth minimal surfaces to the discrete analogues for minimal surfaces, and use it to create global examples of discrete minimal nets with high degree of symmetry. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 53A70; Secondary 53A10 1.

arxiv-2205-13387.title: Coalgebraic Fuzzy geometric logic
arxiv-2205-13387.creator: Litan Kumar Das Department of Mathematics Jadavpur University, Kolkata, India, Kumar Sankar Ray ECSU, Indian Statistical Institute, Kolkata, India, Prakash Chandra Mali Department of Mathematics Jadavpur University, Kolkata, India
arxiv-2205-13387.description: Abstract The paper aims to develop a framework for coalgebraic fuzzy geometric logic by adding modalities to the language of fuzzy geometric logic. Using the methods of coalgebra, the modal operators are introduced in the language of fuzzy geometric logic. To define the modal operators, we introduce a notion of fuzzy-open predicate lifting.

arxiv-2206-06254.description: Abstract The public, all-sky surveys Gaia and TESS provide the ability to identify new young associations and determine their ages. These associations enable study of planetary evolution by providing new opportunities to discover young exoplanets. A young association was recently identified by Tang et al. and Fürnkranz et al. using astrometry from Gaia (called “Group-X” by the former).

arxiv-2305-00579.title: RAPID: Autonomous Multi-Agent Racing using Constrained Potential Dynamic Games
arxiv-2305-00579.creator: Yixuan Jia, Maulik Bhatt, Negar Mehr
arxiv-2305-00579.description: Abstract In this work, we consider the problem of autonomous racing with multiple agents where agents must interact closely and influence each other to compete. We model interactions among agents through a game-theoretical framework and propose an efficient algorithm for tractably solving the resulting game in real time.

arxiv-2305-08896.title: The connection between nonzero density and spontaneous symmetry breaking for interacting scalars
arxiv-2305-08896.creator: Alberto Nicolis, Alessandro Podo, Luca Santoni
arxiv-2305-08896.description: Abstract We consider U ⁡ ( 1 ) {\rm U}(1) -symmetric scalar quantum field theories at zero temperature. At nonzero charge densities, the ground state of these systems is usually assumed to be a superfluid phase, in which the global symmetry is spontaneously broken along with Lorentz boosts and time translations.

arxiv-2306-13338.title: Noise-induced, ac-stabilized sine-Gordon breathers: Emergence and statistics
arxiv-2306-13338.creator: Duilio De Santis, Claudio Guarcello, Bernardo Spagnolo, Angelo Carollo, Davide Valenti
arxiv-2306-13338.description: Abstract Noisy and ac forcing can cooperatively lead to the emergence of sine-Gordon breathers robust to dissipation. This phenomenon is studied, for both Neumann and periodic boundary conditions (NBC and PBC, respectively), at different values of the main system parameters, such as the noise intensity and the ac frequency-amplitude pair.

arxiv-2308-04686.title: Orthogonality catastrophe and quantum speed limit for dynamical quantum phase transition
arxiv-2308-04686.creator: Zheng-Rong Zhu, Bin Shao, Jian Zou, Lian-Ao Wu
arxiv-2308-04686.description: Abstract We investigate the orthogonality catastrophe and quantum speed limit in the Creutz model for dynamical quantum phase transitions. We demonstrate that exact zeros of the Loschmidt echo can exist in finite-size systems for specific discrete values. We highlight the role of the zero-energy mode when analyzing quench dynamics near the critical point.

arxiv-2507-11670.title: Integrable discretisations of the noncommutative NLS equation
arxiv-2507-11670.creator: S. Konstantinou-Rizos, P. Xenitidis
arxiv-2507-11670.description: Abstract We show how to derive noncommutative versions of integrable partial difference equations using Darboux transformations. As an illustrative example, we use the nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) system. We derive a noncommutative nonlinear Schrödinger equation and we construct its integrable discretisations via the compatibility condition of Darboux transformations around the square.

arxiv-2511-12757.title: Which Way from B to A: The role of embedding geometry in image interpolation for Stable Diffusion
arxiv-2511-12757.creator: Nicholas Karris, Luke Durell, Javier E. Flores, Tegan Emerson
arxiv-2511-12757.description: Abstract It can be shown that Stable Diffusion has a permutation-invariance property with respect to the rows of Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) embedding matrices. This inspired the novel observation that these embeddings can naturally be interpreted as point clouds in a Wasserstein space rather than as matrices in a Euclidean space.

pmc-10672444.title: Comparative Study of the Co-Occurring Alternaria and Colletotrichum Species in the Production of Citrus Leaf Spot
pmc-10672444.creator: Mengying Lei, Congyi Zhu, Luoye Li, Jiangshan Liu, Jiashang Liu, Feng Huang
pmc-10672444.description: Both of the two citrus diseases, Alternaria brown spot (ABS) and Anthracnose, caused by Alternaria and Colletotrichum spp., respectively, can produce leaf lesions which are hard to differentiate. These two diseases have been confused as causal agents of brown spot for over a decade in China.

pmc-10740033.title: Physicochemical properties of ultrasound-pretreated pea starch and its inclusion complexes with lauric acid
pmc-10740033.creator: Liuyang Xiao, Yingtao Yu, Xiaofan Yang, Zhaojun Wei, Lihong Han
pmc-10740033.description: Highlights•Ultrasound pretreatment (UPT) affected the morphology and structure of pea starch.•The ultrasonic temperature altered the chain disruption points of pea starch.•UPT at higher temperatures increased the number of linear chains and amylose content.•UPT enhanced the complexation ability of pea starch with lauric acid.

pmc-11319485.title: Antibiotic resistance gene dynamics in the commensal infant gut microbiome over the first year of life
pmc-11319485.creator: Pål Trosvik, Hanna Theodora Noordzij, Eric Jacques de Muinck
pmc-11319485.description: Colonization of the infant gut is an important developmental process characterized by high carriage of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and high abundances of pathobionts. The horizontal transfer of ARGs to pathogenic bacteria represents a major public health concern. However, there is still a paucity of longitudinal studies surveilling ARGs in healthy infant guts at high temporal resolution.

pmc-11392163.title: The professionalism of ChatGPT in the field of surgery: low or high level?
pmc-11392163.creator: Haiyang Wu, Wanqing Li, Xiaofeng Chen, Cheng Li
pmc-11392163.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ilization concerning breast carcinoma, GPT-4.0 not only exhibits superiority concerning quality and pertinence but also manifests remarkable efficacy in practical implementation, notably in contrast to its predecessor, GPT-3.5. With the utilization of ChatGPT escalates, it is foreseeable that healthcare professionals and potentially individuals directly affected by medical conditions or their caregivers, will resort to this application for insights on disease prognostication, particularly in challenging prognostic scenarios2,3. Thus, the importance of this study deserves to be recognized.

pmc-11463755.title: Quantification of threats to bats at localized spatial scales for conservation and management
pmc-11463755.creator: Brian M. Myers, Drew C. Stokes, Kristine L. Preston, Robert N. Fisher, Amy G. Vandergast
pmc-11463755.description: In a rapidly changing world, where species conservation needs vary by local habitat, concentrated conservation efforts at small spatial scales can be critical. Bats provide an array of value to the ecosystems they inhabit; many bat species are also of conservation concern.

pmc-11614272.title: Liver tumor segmentation method combining multi-axis attention and conditional generative adversarial networks
pmc-11614272.creator: Jiahao Liao, Hongyuan Wang, Hanjie Gu, Yinghui Cai
pmc-11614272.description: In modern medical imaging-assisted therapies, manual annotation is commonly employed for liver and tumor segmentation in abdominal CT images. However, this approach suffers from low efficiency and poor accuracy. With the development of deep learning, automatic liver tumor segmentation algorithms based on neural networks have emerged, for the improvement of the work efficiency.

pmc-12359536.title: Are loneliness and social network size mediators between childhood adversity and depressive symptoms? A cross-sectional replication study in Ethiopia
pmc-12359536.creator: Paula Gerbig, Matthias Alexander Reinhard, Henok Ababu, Stephanie Rek, Benedikt L Amann, Kristina Adorjan, Mubarek Abera, Frank Padberg, Andrea Jobst
pmc-12359536.description: Abstract Introduction Loneliness and adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) constitute significant risk factors for mental disorders, with loneliness emerging as a serious global public health concern. Recent research highlights the role of loneliness as a potential link between early life adversities and current psychopathology. However, most studies have been conducted in high-income, highly individualistic countries.

pmc-12555505.title: 11.K. Round table: Placing European patients and providers at the center of decision-making in oral health policies
pmc-12555505.creator: Organised by: Technical University of Berlin (Germany), Chair persons: Ruth Waitzberg (Germany), Pauline Vassallo (EUPHA-OH)
pmc-12555505.description: Despite its critical role in overall well-being, oral health (OH) remains insufficiently integrated into many health systems and warrants greater prioritization. Efforts to strengthen OH integration into European health systems are gaining momentum, creating a window of opportunity to involve both the population and healthcare providers in decision-making.

pmc-13677075.title: A Chiral Virus‐Like Nanoplatform That Broadly Mediates Antibiotic Delivery to the Brain for Bacterial Meningitis Therapy
pmc-13677075.creator: Qianqian Xu, Xuting Zheng, Huinan Tong, Ying Liu, Xiaoxi Fan, Miao Xu, Ziyan Zhang, Li Zhang, Mingyan Liu, Ting Du, Heran Li, Guojun Liu
pmc-13677075.description: Blood‐brain barrier (BBB) preserves brain homeostasis yet restricts therapeutics; in bacterial meningitis, antibiotics’ limited penetration impairs delivery to the parenchyma and cerebrospinal fluid, constraining efficacy and motivating strategies to overcome the barrier. To address this, we developed a chiral virus‐mimicking mesoporous silica nanostructure (CVSN) functionalized with L‐alanine for antibiotic delivery.
